EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
US President Trump has definitively rejected Iran's latest peace proposal, describing it as "garbage" and signaling a heightened possibility of renewed military action, including potential bombing of identified targets or a resumption of operations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Concurrently, the Wall Street Journal revealed that the UAE secretly conducted airstrikes inside Iran in early April, indicating a broader regional willingness to engage militarily with Tehran. The Israel-Lebanon border remains a critical flashpoint following the death of an IDF reservist due to a Hezbollah drone attack, underscoring ongoing, lethal cross-border hostilities.

IRAN
The diplomatic landscape with the US is in severe disarray. US President Trump rejected Iran's latest peace proposal, calling it "stupid," "garbage," and "unacceptable," and claimed Iran initially agreed to remove 60% enriched uranium but later reneged. Trump is reportedly considering resuming "Project Freedom" to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or conducting airstrikes on 25% of identified targets. He plans to meet with his National Security Team today to discuss options, stating, "if a deal is not made, we will hit Iran in a way they have never seen." Trump also expressed the view that Iran lacks the technology to remove its enriched uranium from damaged facilities and alluded to regime change already occurring due to the conflict.

Iranian officials, including Parliament Speaker Qalibaf and Supreme Leader's advisor Velayati, responded defiantly. Qalibaf stated that Iranian armed forces are "ready to deliver a crushing response to any aggression" and "prepared for every option," warning enemies they "will be surprised." Velayati declared, "We defeated you on the battlefield; so don't imagine you'll win through diplomacy." Iranian state media indicated Tehran rejected the US proposal as it implied "full surrender." Iran denies agreeing to remove enriched uranium, stating it only proposed dilution to 3.7% and 20% under IAEA supervision, and demands a specific timeframe for the release of frozen funds. The head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization stated nuclear technology and enrichment are not on the agenda for talks. Russia affirmed that US demands for the destruction of Iranian nuclear facilities contradict the Non-Proliferation Treaty.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the United Arab Emirates (UAE) secretly carried out airstrikes in Iran in early April, including an attack on the Lavan Island oil refinery, with the Pentagon reportedly "satisfied" despite a declared ceasefire. Iran's National Security and Foreign Policy Committee warned against an "UAE-Israel axis" in the region.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, with only nine container ships reportedly transiting in the past 60 days. Iran asserts sovereignty over submarine internet cables in the strait. Qalibaf claimed Iran could strike any vessel from Semnan, Tehran, or Mashhad. Aramco's CEO estimated that even if the strait reopens today, market rebalance would take months, possibly extending to 2027 if delayed further. Belgium and France announced their intention to join a British initiative to clear naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

The US Treasury Department imposed sanctions on 12 individuals and entities involved in facilitating Iranian oil shipments to China, a move China opposes. The UK also sanctioned 12 individuals and entities linked to Iran for "hostile acts."

Internally, Iran executed Erfan Shakour-zadeh, accused of spying for the Mossad and CIA. The assets of former national football star Ali Karimi, an outspoken regime opponent, were confiscated. Iran's Minister of Communications attributed internet restrictions to "war conditions," noting the implementation of "Internet Pro" for businesses, which allows privileged access. Reconstruction work is underway on the B1 Bridge between Tehran and Karaj, which was damaged in a previous US attack.

ISRAEL
An IDF reservist, Warrant Officer (res.) Alexander Glovanyov, 47, from Petah Tikva, was killed on May 11 by a Hezbollah explosive drone near the Lebanon border. Three other IDF soldiers were lightly injured in a separate Hezbollah drone attack in southern Lebanon on May 12.

The IDF conducted operations in southern Lebanon, killing two Hezbollah operatives in a building near Israeli forces on May 11, and striking a rocket launcher and its crew on a truck after they fired rockets at IDF troops. Israeli Air Force (IAF) strikes were reported in Al-Rihan, Kafr Fila, Jarjouaa, and Zawtar al-Gharbiya in southern Lebanon. In Gaza, IDF’s 188th Brigade and Yahalom special engineering unit destroyed four Hamas tunnels, totaling approximately four kilometers, one of which was previously used to hold hostages.

The home front experienced alerts, including a false alarm for hostile aircraft intrusion in Majdal Shams and sirens in Neve Yam triggered by an interceptor launched against a surface-to-air missile fired by Hezbollah at an IAF drone over southern Lebanon. Reports indicated numerous American refueling planes at Ben Gurion Airport, with an Israeli official calling it effectively a "US military base." A security incident in Kibbutz Lahav involved a suspect breaching a barrier, with a security officer firing warning shots. Explosive ordnance was found on Tel Aviv's northern cliff beach, leading to its closure.

Politically, the Knesset approved a law (93 votes in favor) allowing military courts to impose the death penalty on October 7th terrorists, explicitly preventing their release in future hostage deals. Finance Minister Smotrich advocated for transferring additional West Bank territories from Areas A and B to Area C, a move described by his associates as an effective cancellation of the Oslo Accords. Prime Minister Netanyahu is scheduled to hold a security meeting today following Iran's rejection of the US proposal and also defended his choice for the next Mossad chief, Roman Gofman, amidst internal opposition.

An IDF soldier was sentenced to 21 days in military prison for desecrating a Virgin Mary statue in Debel, southern Lebanon, while the soldier who filmed the act received a 14-day sentence. An IAF helicopter experienced a technical malfunction, landing in southern Lebanon during a casualty evacuation mission, but was later repaired and safely returned to base. President Herzog acknowledged the significant challenge posed by the drone threat to IDF forces.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In the Gaza Strip, the IDF's 188th Brigade and Yahalom special engineering unit successfully destroyed four Hamas tunnel routes, collectively spanning approximately four kilometers. One of these tunnels was confirmed to have been used for holding hostages.

In the West Bank, the European Union approved new sanctions against "violent Israeli settlers" and associated organizations. The sanctioned entities include three Israeli citizens and four organizations: Nachala, Amana, Hashomer Yosh, and Regavim, along with right-wing activist Daniella Weiss. At the Kalandia checkpoint, Border Police neutralized a terrorist who opened fire on forces. Nazmi Abu Bakr was convicted by a military court for the intentional killing of Sergeant First Class Amit Ben Yigal in Ya'bad in May 2020. Hamas has called on Palestinians to intensify military operations in response to Israeli actions in the West Bank.

LEBANON
Hezbollah continued its aggressive operations against Israeli forces, launching multiple rockets and explosive drones into southern Lebanon. Two explosive drones struck unmanned engineering vehicles, causing damage but no injuries. An Israeli Air Force drone operating over southern Lebanon was targeted by a Hezbollah surface-to-air missile, which was successfully intercepted by an Israeli missile near Neve Yam, triggering sirens. Three IDF soldiers were lightly injured in a Hezbollah explosive drone attack. The previous day, Warrant Officer (res.) Alexander Glovanyov, 47, was killed by a Hezbollah explosive drone near the border. Hezbollah also claimed a rocket attack on a newly established Israeli command center in Al-Bayada and reportedly made automated calls to residents of Kiryat Shmona, instructing them to evacuate.

In response, the IDF conducted strikes in southern Lebanon. Israeli Air Force eliminated two Hezbollah operatives identified in a building near Israeli forces, which was being used to advance attacks. The IDF also struck a rocket launcher and its crew on a truck after they fired at Israeli forces. Press TV reported six civilians killed and several wounded in Israeli attacks across southern Lebanon, with specific strikes reported in Kafr Fila, Jarjouaa, Zawtar al-Gharbiya, and Al-Rihan. Lebanese sources reported two fatalities in an Israeli vehicle strike in Al-Dweir.

An Israeli Air Force helicopter encountered a technical malfunction and was unable to take off after landing in southern Lebanon to evacuate wounded soldiers. Another helicopter was dispatched for the evacuation, and the original helicopter was later repaired and departed safely. The Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called on the US envoy to pressure Israel to halt its "recurrent violations" of the ceasefire. Hezbollah Secretary General Sheikh Naim Qassem reiterated that Hezbollah's priority is confronting Israeli aggression and stated they would not revert to the terms of the previous Lebanon-Israel ceasefire agreement.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Iraq, conflicting reports emerged regarding the presence of unauthorized military bases. Iraq's Joint Operations Command explicitly denied the existence of any unauthorized forces or bases in Iraqi territory, specifically in the Karbala desert. However, Shargh and Naya channels reported that a secret US-Israeli base is located in the Al-Nakheeb desert in western Iraq, with US CENTCOM allegedly conducting 24-hour reconnaissance over strategic areas including Al-Nakheeb, Al-Khaldiyah, and H3. Reports also indicated unidentified warplanes flying over Al-Baladiyat in eastern Baghdad, causing public concern. An Iranian drone attack was reported in Iraqi Kurdistan, specifically in Erbil. The Iraqi-Iranian security committee met in Baghdad, emphasizing the importance of enhanced security coordination, border control, and preventing infiltration by terrorist or armed groups. Four individuals identified as members of Al-Joulani's gangs were killed by ISIS gunfire in Hasaka, Syria.

In Syria, Ahmad Al-Joulani, leader of the transitional government, reshuffled his cabinet, replacing ministers of information and agriculture, and several provincial governors, including his own brother from the position of Secretary-General of the Presidency. These changes occur amidst economic pressures and criticisms of government performance.

GULF STATES
The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has been implicated in covert military actions against Iran. The Wall Street Journal reported that the UAE secretly conducted strikes inside Iran in early April, including an attack on the Lavan Island oil refinery, which occurred during the declared ceasefire between the US and Iran. The Pentagon reportedly expressed "satisfaction" with these actions. Iran's National Security and Foreign Policy Committee criticized Bahrain and the UAE for being "on the wrong path" and warned against the formation of an "UAE-Israel axis" in the region. The UAE Foreign Ministry also issued a statement confirming the hijacking of an oil tanker off the Yemeni coast, describing it as a direct threat to maritime security. President Mohammed bin Zayed of the UAE spoke with Ukrainian President Zelensky.

Qatar's Foreign Minister engaged in telephone discussions with his Kuwaiti counterpart regarding the Iran-US ceasefire, stressing the importance for all parties to engage in ongoing mediation efforts to resolve the crisis through peaceful means and achieve a lasting agreement.

Regarding maritime transit through the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters, citing official data, reported that oil tankers from Qatar, the UAE, and Iraq are still navigating the strait, albeit on a limited, case-by-case basis, often with explicit security coordination and, at times, with Iranian approval and deactivated tracking systems.

Yemen's Deputy Foreign Minister stated that the "no war, no peace" status quo with Saudi Arabia is no longer acceptable and that Saudi delays in achieving peace will compel Sana'a to consider other options.

In Bahrain, citizens reportedly clashed with Al Khalifa gangs in protest against citizenship revocations and the arrest of Shia clerics accused of supporting Iran in its conflict with the US-Israeli axis.

US President Trump commented that "no one expected Saudi, Qatar, and UAE to be attacked," calling Iran's actions "a big mistake."

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Trump Rejects Iranian Proposal & Threatens Military Action:** US President Trump explicitly rejected Iran's latest peace proposal, labeling it "garbage" and "stupid," and announced he is considering resuming "Project Freedom" for the Strait of Hormuz or bombing 25% of identified targets in Iran.
2.  **UAE Secretly Strikes Iran:** The Wall Street Journal reported that the United Arab Emirates secretly conducted airstrikes inside Iran, including on the Lavan Island oil refinery, in early April, with the Pentagon's tacit approval.
3.  **Iran Warns of "Crushing Response":** Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf declared that Iran's armed forces are "ready to deliver a crushing response" to any aggression and "prepared for every option," warning of "surprise."
4.  **IDF Reservist Killed in Hezbollah Drone Attack:** Warrant Officer (res.) Alexander Glovanyov, 47, an IDF reservist, was killed by a Hezbollah explosive drone near the Lebanon border on May 11. Three other IDF soldiers were lightly injured in a separate drone attack on May 12.
5.  **EU Sanctions Israeli Settlers:** The European Union approved new sanctions against "violent Israeli settlers" and associated organizations in the West Bank, sanctioning three individuals and four groups (Nachala, Amana, Hashomer Yosh, Regavim, and Daniella Weiss).
6.  **Knesset Approves Death Penalty for Oct 7 Terrorists:** The Israeli Knesset passed a law enabling the death penalty for October 7th terrorists, explicitly prohibiting their release in any future hostage exchange deals.
7.  **Iranian Aircraft Sheltered in Pakistan:** CBS News reported that Pakistan, acting as a mediator, quietly allowed Iranian military aircraft, including an RC-130 intelligence plane, to shelter at Nur Khan Air Force Base in early April to protect them from potential US airstrikes.
8.  **Secret US-Israeli Base in Iraq:** Iraqi and Iranian aligned sources (Shargh, Naya) reported the existence of a secret US-Israeli military base in the Al-Nakheeb desert in western Iraq, with US CENTCOM conducting 24-hour reconnaissance. The Iraqi Joint Operations Command, however, denied this.
9.  **Strait of Hormuz Blockade Continues:** The Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed to commercial container traffic, with only nine ships reportedly passing in the last 60 days, fueling discussions about military options to reopen it.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are extremely high following US President Trump's definitive rejection of Iran's peace proposal and his explicit statements about considering renewed military action, including airstrikes and forcefully reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's defiant rhetoric, vowing a "crushing response" and "surprise" to any aggression, sets a collision course for a potential new direct conflict. The revelation of secret UAE airstrikes in Iran during a supposed ceasefire period underscores a volatile regional environment where military engagement is already occurring below the surface.

Active flashpoints include the Iran-US/Israel direct confrontation (over the nuclear program or Strait of Hormuz), the Israel-Lebanon border (daily exchanges with lethal outcomes, as seen with the IDF casualty), and the Strait of Hormuz (risk of military intervention to break the blockade). Reports of a secret US-Israeli base in Iraq and an Iranian drone strike in Iraqi Kurdistan suggest a burgeoning proxy conflict in Iraq.

Military posture changes include the US consideration of significant military operations against Iran, Iran's declared readiness for all options, and Israel's extended reservist call-up. Red lines are clearly drawn by the US and Israel regarding Iran's nuclear program (specifically 60% enriched uranium and refusal to transfer it) and by Iran regarding its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** has signaled a hardening stance against Iran, with President Trump rejecting Iran's peace proposal and contemplating renewed military action. The US Treasury imposed sanctions on 12 individuals and entities for their role in facilitating Iranian oil shipments to China. Trump is scheduled to visit China this week, with Iran on the agenda for discussions with President Xi Jinping.

**China** has expressed opposition to the newly imposed US sanctions on its companies concerning Iran, vowing to protect its businesses from what it deems "illegal and unilateral restrictions."

The **European Union** approved new sanctions targeting "violent Israeli settlers" and organizations operating in the West Bank, sanctioning three individuals and four groups, including Nachala, Amana, Hashomer Yosh, Regavim, and Daniella Weiss. The French Foreign Minister welcomed these sanctions.

The **United Kingdom** is experiencing internal political turmoil within the Labour party, with calls for Prime Minister Keir Starmer's resignation. Starmer emphasized Britain's non-involvement in the war with Iran, focusing on the domestic economic impact of fuel prices. The UK also imposed sanctions on 12 individuals and entities linked to Iran for "hostile acts." Belgium and France will join a UK initiative to clear naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

**Russia's** Ambassador to Vienna, Mikhail Ulyanov, stated that the US demand for the destruction of Iranian nuclear facilities contradicts the Non-Proliferation Treaty. Russia is also expanding its drone factory and exporting parts to Iran.

**Pakistan** continues its role as a mediator between Iran and the US, actively working to draft a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at ending the conflict and facilitating broader dialogue. It was also reported that Pakistan allowed Iranian military aircraft to shelter at Nur Khan Air Force Base in early April to protect them from potential US airstrikes.

**Qatar** stressed the necessity of continued dialogue and mediation to achieve a lasting agreement and prevent further escalation in the region.

**Kazakhstan's** President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev offered his country's assistance in resolving the Iranian nuclear issue, should international agreements be reached.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
**Contradictions and Unverified Claims:** A significant contradiction exists regarding Iran's nuclear negotiations. While US sources (Trump, Al Jazeera) claim Iran initially agreed to remove/dilute enriched uranium but later reversed, Iranian sources (Tasnim, Shargh) explicitly deny any agreement to remove enriched uranium from the country, stating willingness only to dilute it under IAEA supervision. This directly impacts the perceived sincerity and progress of negotiations.

The existence of a secret US-Israeli base in the Al-Nakheeb desert, western Iraq, reported by Shargh and Naya, is explicitly denied by Iraq's Joint Operations Command. This remains an unverified claim from sources often aligned with Iranian interests.

Press TV's report of "six civilians killed" in Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon lacks specific context and independent verification, contrasting with other reports that mention two Hezbollah operatives killed in one strike and IDF casualties.

Trump's claim that Kurds "disappointed us" by not delivering weapons into Iran is unverified and runs counter to established narratives of US-Kurdish cooperation.

**Propaganda Indicators:** The rhetoric from both US and Iranian leadership exhibits strong propaganda elements. Trump's labeling of Iran's proposal as "garbage" and threats of unprecedented military strikes, alongside Iranian officials' declarations of "crushing responses" and "surprises," are designed to project strength, demoralize the adversary, and rally domestic support. The messaging campaign of "Jan Fada" (Sacrifice for leader) in Iran, reportedly sent to individuals who did not register, including deceased persons, indicates a concerted effort to artificially inflate public support for the Supreme Leader. The implementation of "Internet Pro" in Iran, providing preferential internet access to certain businesses while restricting general access, highlights internal digital inequality and is a method of information control during wartime.

**Reporting Gaps:** Specific details regarding the alleged UAE airstrikes in Iran, beyond the Lavan Island refinery, are lacking. The full contents and precise demands of both the US and Iranian peace proposals are not fully disclosed, making it challenging to thoroughly assess the actual points of disagreement. The current status and potential timeline for the resumption of "Project Freedom" to reopen the Strait of Hormuz are unclear, with Trump only stating he is "considering" it. The nature and origin of "unidentified warplanes" reported over Baghdad remain unknown, raising concerns but lacking definitive attribution.
